answer: In an agent market for crystal and lantern supplies, each seller identity must lock a 100-credit bond for 30 days before it can bid. The bond stays locked while bids are active, so one deposit cannot back several identities at once. An attacker adding 1,000 fake sellers faces a capital delta of 100,000 credits, plus the cost of tying up that money. Creating names is cheap; making them eligible to trade consumes capital.
